goal: Boost small business in SoMa without slowing Bay Bridge traffic

options.title: SoMa alleys: Clementina + Minna + Natoma
options.rationale: This plan adds 651 walking commuters and is valued at about $22.3M per year, mostly from mobility and health. However, the model shows revenue down $18,535 and total delay up 60.33 hours, and the model does not report Bay Bridge traffic separately, so it fails both the small-business goal and the no-slowdown goal.

options.title: Clementina + Minna + Stevenson with $5 Bay Bridge (I-80) charge
options.rationale: This is the only plan that meets both goals. Revenue rises $9,948, total delay falls 773.53 hours, and the plan is valued at about $35.1M per year. The costs are 3,297 fewer car commuters, a mobility value of -$25.7M per year, and a rent pressure index that rises slightly (+0.03). The $5 charge is my assumed level, not a tested optimum, and the model does not report Bay Bridge traffic on its own.

options.title: Main Street + Clementina + Ellis
options.rationale: This plan has the most new social ties (250) and a value of about $19.9M per year, driven by mobility, health and social gains. Revenue is essentially flat (-$180) and delay rises 193.59 hours, so it does little for small business and risks slowing traffic. I'd treat it as a community-focused fallback, not a Bay Bridge-safe option.
